Theme

School & learning · Work & responsibility

chart noun

a diagram of figures or facts

also charts, graph, diagram, table (of figures), bar chart, pie chart

modern

M-O s.v. parts: table (in book), chart (Trappen 1843)

tabula, tabulae f.

noun, first declension

a chart or table (in a book or report)

Classically a board, a writing tablet, a painting, a map (tabula picta), a list or account; the chart or table of a book is a modern use of it.

Other words

  • dēscrīptiō, dēscrīptiōnis f. — a diagram, drawing, plan

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.38: numerīs aut dēscrīptiōnibus; Vitr. 8.2, of maps of the world (Lewis & Short)

    A drawing out: Cicero’s word for the figures of the geometers. Far more often it means a description in words, or an arrangement (Lewis & Short).

  • cōnspectus, cōnspectūs m. — a table giving an overview

    noun, fourth declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. parts: table (in book), chart (Trappen 1843)

    Classically a view or survey (see survey, an overview); a synopsis in Gellius.

Examples

  • ratiōnem illī sententiae suae nōn ferē reddēbant, nisi quid erat numerīs aut dēscrīptiōnibus explicandum

    they hardly ever gave reasons for their views, unless something had to be explained with numbers or diagramsCic. Tusc. 1.38

See also map, survey.

SourcesLewis & Short: tabula · Lewis & Short: descriptio · Lewis & Short: conspectus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. parts: table (in book), chart.
